thread.title: Following a monster fiscal Q4 2017 , Apple ( AAPL ) did not

author: D.M. Martins Research
title: Following a monster fiscal Q4 2017 , Apple ( AAPL ) did not
text:
Following a monster fiscal Q4 2017 , Apple ( AAPL ) did not follow through with an equally impressive holiday quarter.
The Cupertino company reported revenues of $88.3 billion that beat consensus by $670 million and accounted for the largest YoY increase since the September 2015 quarter. EPS of $3.89 also exceeded estimates, but by a less exciting four cents. Revenue guidance for the upcoming quarter came in light, which could very well pressure the stock in the very short term. I calculate that management's outlook points at EPS expectations of $2.66 for fiscal Q2 2018, which falls significantly below consensus $2.84.

Image credit 
In my earnings preview and after observing data on device activation, I predicted softness in smartphone sales this quarter. Because the iPhone X was not released until November 2017, the adoption of newly-introduced devices, including models 8 and 8 Plus, happened much more slowly than in previous years. The results released this evening confirmed my fears, as units sold of 77.3 million came in materially lower than the expected 81.5 million.
iPhone ASP of $796, however, was much larger than consensus $755, possibly suggesting that weakness in the higher-end model was not the main driver of the segment's unimpressive unit sales performance. A couple of more likely reasons might include 1) cannibalization of Apple's mid-range devices and/or 2) a weaker refresh cycle than some might have been expecting. I will be curious to learn more on this topic as the news continue to be digested over the next couple of days.
